title: Batch accumulation memory ripple — postmortem and runbook draft
content:
Incident overview

Incident id: SR-2025-02-17-01
Severity: Sev2 (customer-facing latency spikes, a subset of dedicated hosts OOM)
Primary affected surface: serving-runtime multitenant pools (continuous batching scheduler + prefix KV cache)
Summary: During a scheduled traffic spike for several PLG customers, a combination of scheduler parameter drift and a KV cache TTL calculation bug allowed microbatches to grow unbounded for a subset of requests. The apparent trigger was opportunistic merging in the continuous-batching pipeline, which increased working set retention and then caused cascading evictions and memory pressure across hosts. Several hosts hit OOM and restarted, producing transient errors and elevated tail latency for about 18 minutes.

Detection and timeline (UTC)
- 2025-02-17 15:03 — Alert: host_group-east-3 memory_usage > 90% (SRE auto-alert).
- 15:05 — Pod restarts observed on 3/24 hosts in the pool; bump in 5xx rate and client-visible latency.
- 15:07 — On-call paged. Initial hypothesis: allocation spike from model quantization path rollback (ruled out).
- 15:10 — Observed sudden rise in average microbatch size per worker from 12 -> 46 tokens/req equivalent.
- 15:12 — KV cache evictions/sec for the pool rose 20x; eviction storms correlated with host heap growth.
- 15:17 — Mitigation: temporarily reduced continuous-batching max_wait_ms from 60ms -> 20ms and scaled pool + removed bursting ai-inference route. Memory pressure reduced on remaining hosts.
- 15:21 — Deployed emergency patch to avoid opportunistic merge across tenant isolation boundary (hotfix merged 15:34).
- 15:40 — All hosts back to normal baselines; follow-up window declared 24h.

What we saw (observables)
- Metrics: batch_size.p50 jumped from 14 -> 32 and p95 to 64 on affected hosts.
- Heap usage per worker increased steadily (heap_growth ~ 40% over 6 minutes) until the host OOM Killed process.
- Evictions/sec for KV cache went from ~3 -> 65 during the spike.
- Queue depth for continuous batching grew to 200+ (target <= 50).
- Logs contained repeated entries: "merge_candidate_wait_exceeded -> merging permitted" and then later "kv_cache_reserve_failed: OOM" before OOM kill.

Root cause analysis (short)
1) Scheduler parameter drift: a recent change (PR #2378) adjusted the opportunistic-merge backoff heuristic. Under bursty PLG traffic shapes, this made merges more aggressive than intended, allowing larger accumulated microbatches to be formed before processing.
2) KV cache TTL misestimation: a separate bug in the KV cache size estimator used fractional TTL values that rounded down for short-lived prefixes, causing entries to linger longer than their intended eviction window under heavy access patterns. This increased working set size.
3) Feedback amplification: larger microbatches increased per-request KV retention time (more KV entries referenced per request), which caused more frequent evictions and fragmentation, which in turn triggered internal memory accounting edge cases and latent allocation spikes.
4) Insufficient defensive limits: there was no hard circuit to abort merges when queue depth > 150 or when host_mem_headroom < 10%.

Contributing factors
- Recent merge heuristic change lacked a load-pattern test for bursty PLG simulation.
- Eviction accounting and reserve calls were optimistic and did not fail fast when reserves couldn't be satisfied.
- Monitoring thresholds for eviction storms were set too high, so early signs were not paged.
- Canary coverage for dedicated pools did not include the exact tenant mix that triggered the pattern.

Immediate mitigations performed during incident
- Reduced max_wait_ms for continuous batching from 60 -> 20 to reduce accumulation window (rollback of merge aggressiveness).
- Scaled the affected pool by +30% capacity to absorb the extra memory pressure while mitigations were applied.
- Disabled the new opportunistic merge path for the rollout channel (config gate).
- Restarted 3 OOM'd hosts and drained a further 4 to rebalance cache pressure.

Permanent fixes and planned changes (action items)
1) Scheduler hard limits (short term, P0):
   - Add an abort condition in the batching scheduler: do not merge if queue_depth >= 150 or host_memory_headroom < 10%. Owner: Tomoko. ETA: 3 days.
2) KV cache estimator fix (P0):
   - Fix TTL rounding logic so short-lived prefixes use ceil-based reservation and instrument a reserve-failure metric. Owner: Diego. ETA: 1 week.
3) Merge heuristic testing (P1):
   - Add a load test in our CI harness that replays PLG traffic spike shapes that previously reproduced this incident. Owner: Liam. ETA: 2 weeks.
4) Monitoring and alerting (P0):
   - Create an eviction_storm alert (evictions/sec > 20 sustained for 3m) and early queue_depth alert (>= 100 for 2m) that pages SRE. Owner: Aisha. ETA: 72 hours.
5) Canary policy updates (P1):
   - Expand canary tenant diversity for scheduled rollouts to include PLG-like mixes; add deterministic replay scenario. Owner: Product infra. ETA: 3 weeks.
6) Runbook additions (P0):
   - Add explicit emergency steps to the serving-runtime SRE playbook for: immediate merge disable, reducing max_wait_ms, and soft-draining hosts. Drafted below. Owner: Aisha/Tomoko. ETA: 48 hours.

Runbook draft: emergency memory-ripple (serving-runtime)
- Detection:
  - If host_group memory_usage > 85% for 2 consecutive minutes AND evictions/sec > 10, escalate to on-call.
- Immediate actions (first 5 minutes):
  1) Disable opportunistic merges for the affected pool: `rbacctl set-config serving.runtime.merge.enabled=false --pool <pool>`
  2) Reduce continuous batching window: `rbatchctl update --pool <pool> --max_wait_ms 20`
  3) Scale up pool by 25% and enable soft-drain on the 2 highest-heap hosts.
  4) If restarts continue, restart the worker service with `systemctl restart ai-serving-worker` and mark host for manual inspection.
- Post-stabilization (15–60 minutes):
  - Collect heap snapshots from restarted hosts (`/var/log/serving/heap-snapshot-*.prof`) and upload to artifact store.
  - Run the KV cache audit tool: `./tools/kv-audit --pool <pool> --since 20m` and save output to incident ticket.
- Communication
  - Post status update to #sre-incidents and #hosting-notifications channel every 10 minutes until stable.

Diagnostic commands (operational)
- Check average batch size by host: `promql: avg(batch_size) by (host)`
- Evictions per second: `promql: sum(irate(kv_cache_evictions_total[1m])) by (pool)`
- Queue depth: `kubectl exec -c metrics-sidecar <pod> -- curl localhost:9001/metrics | grep batch_queue_depth`
- Reserve failure logs: `rg "reserve_failed|reserve_failure" /var/log/serving/*.log -n`

Testing and validation plan post-fix
- Run the new PLG spike replay in staging 10x across different seed permutations and assert:
  - p95 latency remains within baseline +20%
  - max batch_size < 40 for >99% of requests
  - evictions/sec < 8 sustained
- Add synthetic test that forces reserve_failure and ensures scheduler aborts merges when reserve fails.
- Post-deploy: monitor the new eviction_storm alert for one week; treat any trigger as a P0 and roll back merge heuristic change immediately.

Retrospective notes and learnings
- Merging heuristics are powerful optimizations but need tight guards against tail traffic shapes.
- Cache size estimation must be conservative under contention; optimistic reservations lead to silent working-set growth.
- Guardrails (hard limits + fast-fail reserve) are more reliable than purely heuristic tuning.
- Canary coverage should be explicitly designed for traffic shape diversity rather than just request counts.

Owners and follow-ups (owners listed again)
- Emergency runbook + alerting: Aisha (owner) — ETA 72h
- Hard abort conditions in scheduler: Tomoko — ETA 3d
- KV TTL/reserve fix + metrics: Diego — ETA 1w
- CI replay tests + canary policy changes: Liam / Product Infra — ETA 2–3w

Appendix: short log excerpts (redacted)
- 15:09:03 [worker-12] INFO merge_candidate_wait_exceeded id=0x7f3a queue_depth=173 oldest_wait_ms=84
- 15:09:04 [worker-12] WARN reserve_failed pool=pg-dedicated tenant=plg-x prefix_len=24 want=8192 have=0
- 15:09:05 [kernel] oom-kill: Killed process 4210 (ai-serving) total-vm: 12G anon-rss: 9.4G
- 15:10:11 [metrics] gauge(batch_size): host=host-173 value=58

Notes for follow-up ticket creation
- Create a single Linear ticket that groups scheduler hard-limits + KV reserve fix + alerting (link as parent), then create sub-tasks for each owner.
- Schedule a 1-hour postmortem review with Product Infra and Serving Runtime teams to walk through the CI replay scenarios.

End of document.
